improvement_suggestions.clarity: Redesign every slide for visual hierarchy; replace dense text blocks with graphics, screenshots and bullet points. Fix all typographical and OCR errors and articulate a concise value proposition within the first two slides.
improvement_suggestions.market_opportunity: Add a dedicated market sizing slide (TAM/SAM/SOM) with credible sources, illustrate target customer segments, and explain growth trends that justify the opportunity.
improvement_suggestions.traction: Show concrete KPIs – active users, revenue (ARR), growth rates, churn, NPS, and any paid pilot results. Include a timeline of milestones and demonstrate how the 250‑school pilot translates to revenue.
improvement_suggestions.team: Highlight each founder’s track record of building or scaling a product, include relevant past exits or revenue achievements, and clarify advisory board roles in go‑to‑market execution.
improvement_suggestions.pitch_quality: Adopt a modern, clean deck template; use high‑resolution images, icons, and charts. Keep slides under 20 words and use consistent fonts/colours. Add a clear funding ask and use‑of‑funds slide.
improvement_suggestions.competitive_positioning: Insert a competitor matrix that maps key players, differentiators, and barriers to entry. Explain the unique moat (IP, workflow model, ecosystem) and how you will defend it.

major_agreements: The deck is overly text‑heavy, contains many typographical/OCR errors, and fails to communicate a clear value proposition early.
There is a serious lack of quantitative data – no revenue numbers, unit economics, or market sizing.
The founding team’s academic and advisory credentials are a clear strength.
Competitive positioning and differentiation are virtually absent.

top_strengths: Founders have strong academic and industry credentials, plus advisory support from senior executives.
Five years of R&D and a proven pilot in the Australian yearbook market (250 schools).
Recognition through awards and a documented IP protection strategy.
Existing user base demonstrates early adoption.
top_weaknesses: No financials or revenue projections despite five years of development.
Unclear market size and go‑to‑market strategy.
Slides are text‑heavy, contain numerous typos/OCR errors, and lack visual appeal.
Exit aspirations (acquisition by Google/Apple) appear unrealistic without supporting data.
missing_sections: Detailed financials (historical revenue, unit economics, forecasted ARR).
Key performance metrics (CAC, LTV, churn, NPS).
red_flags: Absence of any concrete revenue or ARR figures after five years of product development.
Bold claim to replace Microsoft Office without any supporting market data.
Outdated content (e.g., 2007 promo video) and repeated OCR/typo errors suggesting low professionalism.
Unrealistic exit targets (Google, Apple, Microsoft) without a clear path.
Opening slides do not convey a clear value proposition or market positioning.
overall_recommendation: The startup is not investment ready at this time. Require substantial additional information on market opportunity, traction metrics, and financials before a funding decision can be made.
